2027-06-30.title: The Twelve Apostles · Wednesday of the sixth week after Pentecost
readings: Servants of God: as having nothing, and yet possessing everything
He appointed twelve, to be with him and to be sent out to proclaim the message
2027-06-30.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps today the commemoration of the Twelve Apostles, the day after the feast of Sts Peter and Paul, with which the Apostles' Fast ended. On Saturday, 3 July, the Church keeps the Dukhrono of Mar Thoma Shleeha, the Apostle of India.
2027-06-30.verse: And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message,
theo: Yesterday the Church celebrated the two great pillars, Peter and Paul, and the Apostles' Fast came to an end. Today, as if gathering the whole family together after the feast, she remembers all the Twelve. St Mark tells how it began: “He went up the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him.” St Luke adds that before choosing them Jesus “spent the night in prayer to God” (Luke 6:12). The call of the Apostles was born in the prayer of the Son to the Father, and it came from his choice, not theirs. The mountain recalls Sinai, where God formed Israel as his people, and the number twelve recalls the twelve tribes: in choosing the Twelve, Jesus was gathering a renewed people of God, the Church. The Book of Revelation sees the end of the story in the heavenly city: “And the wall of the city has twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb” (Revelation 21:14). Every one of us who believes stands on those foundations.

Mark tells us why they were chosen: “And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message, and to have authority to cast out demons.” There are two movements here, and their order matters. First, to be with him; then, to be sent. No one can be sent who has not first been with Jesus, at table, on the road, in prayer, at the foot of the cross. And whoever has truly been with him cannot keep him to himself. Then Mark gives the names, and what a mixture they are: Simon, to whom Jesus gave the name Peter; James and John, the fiery brothers he called Sons of Thunder; Andrew and Philip; Bartholomew, whom our calendar remembered as Mar Barthulmai on 11 June; Matthew, the tax collector; Thomas, who brought the gospel to our land and whose Dukhrono we keep on Saturday; James son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus, remembered as Mar Yuda Thaddai on 19 June; Simon the Cananaean; and Judas Iscariot, “who betrayed him.” Fishermen and a tax collector, quiet men and hot-tempered ones: Jesus did not choose them because they were alike, but made them one around himself. The sad last name reminds us that even one who has been close to the Lord can fall away, and the Church later chose Matthias to take his place among the Twelve.

In the Epistle, St Paul, who was not one of the Twelve but was called by the risen Lord, describes the apostolic life from the inside. “As we work together with him, we urge you also not to accept the grace of God in vain. For he says, ‘At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.’ See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!” The fast is over, but the acceptable time is not; it is always now. Then Paul lists what the work of an apostle cost him: “through great endurance, in afflictions, hardships, calamities, beatings, imprisonments, riots, labors, sleepless nights, hunger.” Tradition tells that almost all of the Twelve gave their lives for Christ. Yet Paul ends with a song of paradoxes: “as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.” St John Chrysostom, who loved Paul dearly, said that the apostles had no house of their own, yet every house of the faithful was open to them, and that this is what it means to have nothing and possess everything (Homilies on Second Corinthians, in substance).

The Church that the Twelve founded is still apostolic. The bishops, gathered around the successor of Peter, are the successors of the Apostles, and the faith we profess is the faith they preached. Our own Church treasures the apostolic faith brought to India by Mar Thoma Shleeha, and lives it in full communion with the Bishop of Rome. But to be apostolic is not only a matter of history and of bishops. Every baptized Christian is called, like the Twelve, to be with Jesus and to be sent. To be with him in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono; to be sent to the office, the field, the classroom and the hospital ward, carrying the message. The fast has ended; the mission has not. Today, at the turning of the month, let us thank God for the Twelve, ask their prayers, and offer ourselves again to be with the Lord and to go where he sends us.
outline: Ask: how much time do I spend with Jesus, and where is he sending me?
Chosen after a night of prayer; the twelve foundations of the new people of God.
The first purpose of the call: friendship and prayer.
Twelve very different men, made one and sent; Thomas who came to our land.
The cost and the joy of the apostolic life; now is the acceptable time.
“to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message”
live: Set aside fifteen minutes each day this week for silent prayer with the Gospel, as the first part of your mission.
Choose one person who does not know Christ or has drifted away, and share a word of faith or an invitation with them before the Dukhrono of St Thomas on Saturday.
Do not receive grace in vain (2 Corinthians 6:1)
Keep one good habit from the Apostles' Fast, a prayer, a small fast or an act of almsgiving, for the rest of the year.
2027-06-30.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, after a night of prayer you called to yourself those whom you wanted, and you appointed the Twelve to be with you and to be sent out to proclaim your message. We thank you for your holy Apostles, the foundations of your Church, and especially for Mar Thoma Shleeha, who brought your gospel to our land. Through their prayers keep us in the apostolic faith and in communion with the successor of Peter. Draw us to be with you in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono, and send us out as your witnesses. When the work is hard, let us be sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing and yet possessing everything in you. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The Twelve were with Jesus at the Last Supper, when he said, Do this in remembrance of me; at every Holy Qurbono the Church, built on the Apostles, does what he commanded them, and the Lord is again with his own.
conn: Luke 6:12–13: Jesus spent the night in prayer on the mountain, and when day came he chose twelve and named them apostles; Mark 3:13–19 is today's account of the same call.

Revelation 21:14: the wall of the heavenly city has twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb; Ephesians 2:20 speaks of the household of God built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets.
Acts 1:26: after the fall of Judas the lot fell on Matthias, and he was added to the eleven apostles; the apostolic ministry continues in the Church.
fathers: The apostles received the gospel for us from the Lord Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ was sent from God; so Christ is from God and the apostles are from Christ. Preaching in country and town, they appointed their first converts, after testing them by the Spirit, to be bishops and deacons of those who would believe (Letter to the Corinthians 42, in substance).

The apostles had nothing, yet they possessed everything: they had no house, yet the houses of all the faithful were open to them; they owned nothing, yet they lacked nothing, because they possessed Christ (Homilies on Second Corinthians, in substance).
magis: Jesus is the Father's emissary. From the beginning of his ministry he called to him those whom he desired and appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out to preach; from then on they would be his emissaries, and in them Christ continues his own mission (in substance).

The Lord Jesus endowed his community with a structure that will remain until the Kingdom is fully achieved: the choice of the Twelve with Peter as their head; representing the twelve tribes of Israel, they are the foundation stones of the new Jerusalem (in substance).
By divine institution the bishops have succeeded to the place of the apostles as shepherds of the Church, so that whoever hears them hears Christ (in substance).

quick: Jesus went up the mountain, called those whom he wanted, and appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out to proclaim the message.
The Twelve were very different men, from Simon Peter to Thomas, who brought the gospel to India, made one around Christ.
Paul describes the apostolic life: now is the acceptable time; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
2027-06-30.action: Spend fifteen minutes with Jesus in prayer today, and then do one thing to share him with someone.
2027-06-30.question: Am I spending enough time with Jesus to be sent by him?

family.explain: Jesus chose twelve friends to be his Apostles. First he wanted them to be with him, to listen to him and to pray with him. Then he sent them out to tell everyone about God's love. They were very different: fishermen, a tax collector, quiet men and loud men. One of them, St Thomas, came all the way to India. Jesus calls us too: to be with him and to share his love.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and our bishops, the successors of the Apostles, and for missionaries everywhere.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we name all twelve Apostles together? Which one would you like to know more about?”

illus: A religious sister from a village near Adoor left home at nineteen with one small suitcase to work among the poor in a mission in central India. For thirty years she taught in a village school and ran a dispensary, often with no electricity and little money. When she came home on leave, a niece asked her, a little sadly, whether she did not regret owning nothing at all. The sister laughed and began to count on her fingers the families who welcomed her into their homes, the children who had become teachers and nurses, the old people who called her their daughter. Then she said: I have no house, but I have a hundred homes. I came with one suitcase and I have more than I can carry. Her niece later found the same idea in St Paul: as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the Twelve to be with you and sent them out to proclaim the good news. Call us to be with you, and send us out as your witnesses, through the prayers of your holy Apostles. Amen.
share: He called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him (Mark 3:13). How did Jesus call me, and how did I come?
to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message (Mark 3:14). Do I spend time with him before I try to work for him?
as having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). What do I possess because I have Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out as your witnesses.
interc: For Pope Leo XIV, the successor of Peter, and for all bishops, the successors of the Apostles, that they may guard and spread the apostolic faith.
For missionaries who have left home and family to proclaim the gospel, that they may be sorrowful yet always rejoicing.
For the Syro-Malankara Church and all the Churches of St Thomas in India, that they may be faithful to the faith of the Apostle.
For Christians who suffer for their faith, as the Apostles did, that they may be strengthened.
For our parish, that we may be with Jesus in prayer and be sent by him into our daily lives.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the foundation of the Apostles. Through their prayers keep us faithful to their teaching, united in their communion, and eager to be sent as they were. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The Syriac word for apostle, meaning one who is sent, from the verb to send; it corresponds to the Greek word apostolos. The plural is Shleeheh, in Malayalam ശ്ലീഹന്മാർ. Mar Thoma Shleeha is St Thomas the Apostle.
kidsaint: Jesus chose twelve friends, and they were not all the same. Peter, Andrew, James and John were fishermen. Matthew collected taxes, and people did not like him. Simon the Cananaean was a man with strong opinions. James and John were so loud and fiery that Jesus called them Sons of Thunder! But Jesus loved them all and taught them to love one another. Thomas, one of them, came all the way to India. Lesson: in Jesus' family, everyone has a place, and we must be friends with those who are different from us.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated Sts Peter and Paul, and today we remember all twelve Apostles together. St Mark tells us: He went up the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him (Mark 3:13). St Luke says that Jesus first spent the night in prayer (Luke 6:12). The Apostles were born from the prayer of Jesus.

Why did he choose them? Mark answers: he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message (Mark 3:14). First, to be with him. Then, to be sent. We cannot give Jesus to others if we have not spent time with him. And if we really have been with him, we cannot keep him to ourselves.

The Twelve were very different: fishermen, a tax collector, fiery brothers, quiet men. Among them was Thomas, who came to our land and whose Dukhrono we keep on Saturday. St Paul tells us what the apostolic life costs and what it gives: as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). And he reminds us: now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation (2 Corinthians 6:2).

The Apostles' Fast is over, but the mission continues. Our bishops, with the successor of Peter, carry on the work of the Twelve, and every one of us is called in our own way. So let us be with Jesus each day in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono, and let us go where he sends us. Holy Apostles of the Lord, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once went up a mountain and called twelve friends to be his Apostles. Can you count them on your fingers? Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James, Thaddaeus, Simon and Judas. They were all different, but Jesus loved each one. First he wanted them to be with him, and then he sent them to tell others about God. Jesus wants you to be with him too, when you pray, and then to go and be kind to others in his name.

intro: Theme: “to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message”
On the commemoration of the Twelve Apostles, the day after the feast of Sts Peter and Paul: called up the mountain, to be with him, to be sent, and having nothing yet possessing everything.

sub: Chosen after a night of prayer.
He called those whom he wanted.
Twelve foundations of a renewed people.
q: And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
points.apply: Thank God today for the moment and the people through whom he called you to faith.

sub: The first purpose of the call.
At table, on the road, at the cross.
q: One thing I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life,
I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
points.apply: Give fifteen minutes each day this week to silent prayer before the Gospel.

sub: Fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot, made one.
Thomas, who came to our land.
Bishops with the successor of Peter, and every baptized Christian.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news,
Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
points.apply: Invite one person to church or share a word of faith before the Dukhrono of St Thomas on Saturday.

sub: Endurance in afflictions, hardships and hunger.
q: The Lord is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.
Then Peter said in reply, “Look, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”
points.apply: Keep one good habit from the Apostles' Fast for the rest of the year.

concl: The Twelve were called to be with Jesus and to be sent; the Church built on them is apostolic still.
Every baptized Christian shares their call: to be with the Lord, and to go where he sends.
2027-06-30.resolve: Be with Jesus each day, and go where he sends you, rich in him though having nothing.
